title: Hitrate Forecast, Lease TTL Policy, and Key Synthesis Playbook for Namespace Caches
creator: Asha Murthy
description: Problem: Our current prefix/kv caching guidance is fragmented and tuned by hand; customers and Dedicated deployments frequently over-provision TTLs which increases token/unit cost. Goal: produce an operational playbook that (1) forecasts per-namespace hit uplift from candidate TTL/lease changes, (2) generates conservative 'lease windows' (per-namespace TTL suggestions) that respect latency SLOs, and (3) prescribes safe key-synthesis rules to avoid high-cardinality explosion and hot-key amplification.
technical_summary: We propose a three-part approach: (A) a lightweight arrival/hotness estimator per namespace that blends recency-weighted counts with burst detection, (B) a parametric hit-projection model that maps lease length to expected hit-rate uplift (using exponential inter-arrival assumption with overdispersion correction), and (C) deterministic key-synthesis constraints (affix bucketing, canonical suffix trimming, and namespace leases) to keep cardinality bounded. The model is intentionally conservative: we calibrate uplift estimates using A/B shadow runs on 10% traffic and a 99th percentile safety multiplier before recommending production applies.
proposed_algorithm:
1) Instrument per-namespace event stream: count unique prefix keys, per-key request frequency (sliding 1h, 6h, 24h windows), and short-term burstiness (peak/median ratio).
2) Estimate arrival process: fit a Poisson rate lambda per key with a negative-binomial overdispersion parameter phi per-namespace to capture bursty workloads.
3) Project hit uplift: for candidate lease L, per-key hit probability ~ 1 - exp(-lambda * L) (corrected for phi -> use 1 - (1 + lambda*L/phi)^(-phi)). Sum weighted by observed key frequency to compute namespace-level expected hit-rate.
4) Cost delta calculation: translate expected saved generator tokens to $ using per-token cost and account for extra memory/eviction churn cost.
5) Safety margin: apply multiplier 0.75 to uplift estimate for initial canaries.
6) Key synthesis rules: canonicalize by removing request-specific UUID suffixes, collapse query-param order, and attach a 4-bit affix hash for low-conflicts; enforce max cardinality thresholds per namespace with automatic fallback to hashed-bucket fallback if exceeded.
policy_tuning_guidance:
- Lease windows: suggest (short, medium, long) windows per namespace where short=100ms-2s, medium=2s-60s, long=60s-10m depending on median inter-arrival.
- Conservative default: prefer medium window for user-facing chat routes, short for rare admin ops.
- Eviction churn control: if eviction rate > 15% and miss rate increases after apply, reduce lease by 25% and re-evaluate.
- Cold-start protection: do not increase lease for namespaces with unique-key growth > 20%/day until shadow run completes.
- Adaptive decay: decouple lease increases from decreases — increases only after 24h stable uplift, decreases can be batched and applied within 2h for cost control.
rollout_plan:
1) Synth-run: run model offline against last 14 days of traffic to produce candidate lease recommendations and expected cost delta. Export results to /dashboards/cost-opt/namespace-forecast.
2) Shadow canary (10% traffic): apply suggested lease changes in shadow mode for 6-12 hours; collect hit, latency, eviction, and memory metrics.
3) Staged apply (per-region): if shadow uplift > safety threshold, apply to 25% region, monitor 24h.
4) Full apply with gradual ramp to 100% over 48h, with auto-rollback gates.
5) Continuous autotune: run nightly re-evaluation and submit PRs to policy repo for human review when suggested changes exceed configured delta thresholds.
rollback_criteria: p95 latency regression > 15% relative to baseline for request latency-sensitive routes
unexpected increase in total memory footprint > 10% for cache nodes
miss rate does not improve after lease increase or increases > 20% compared to baseline
eviction churn causes tail latency spikes (observable in trace sampling)
cardinality explosion: unique keys in namespace > configured upper bound (default 1M)
acceptance_criteria: Model produces stable uplift predictions with median absolute error < 8% against 7-day holdout
Canary run demonstrates no p95 latency regression > 10% and no production errors attributable to cache apply
Policy repo PR with recommendations and automated tests merged
Runbook for rollbacks and emergency mitigation published in Confluence
Dashboard with per-namespace forecast, applied lease, and cost delta visible to ops and PMs

2025-11-25 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented offline synth-run for sample namespaces (chat-rt, rerank, embeddings). Observed uplift 8-12% for chat-rt with medium lease. Preparing shadow canary config.

notes: This ticket focuses strictly on recommendation generation and safe apply/rollback mechanics. Separate follow-ups will address operator UI, RBAC controls for policy applies, and Dedicated deployment packaging. The model intentionally biases conservative to prioritize customer SLOs over aggressive cost wins. Expect iteration after 2-3 customer-canary experiments.
